title: TraceQA baseline
description: A baseline is a saved copy of the components.json files (and crops) of one run, kept in a folder that may be committed. `traceqa diff --against` compares a new run with it. It is only ever written by `traceqa baseline save|promote|alias`, never by extract or diff. Layout: <dir>/<key>/baseline.json (BaselineFile), <dir>/<key>/<target dir>/components.json and, when the saved run had them, crops/.

BaselineFile.description: baseline.json. Holds no storage state, no run.json and no error text, so the folder is safe to commit.

key.description: The folder name: the host of the page (made safe for file names) and 8 hex characters of the SHA-256 of the page address, or the name the person gave.

url.description: The page address with secrets replaced, as in components.json.

fingerprintVersion.description: Ids of a run with another fingerprintVersion cannot be compared; save the baseline again.

promotedAt.description: RFC 3339 timestamp in UTC of the last save or promote.

targets.description: One entry per saved target folder. Targets pair with a run's by dir.

aliases.description: Rename links: a component that was removed from the page under one id and added under another is the same component.

promotions.description: What each save or promote replaced, oldest first. At most the last 20 are kept.

BaselineSource.description: The run a baseline was made from.

engineVersion.description: Or 'unknown' when the run had no run.json.

BaselineAlias.description: Says that the removed component `from` is the added component `to`. A diff then reports one renamed pair (a pairedWith link with reason 'aliased') and the removed, added and paired gates ignore it.

from.description: A component id in the baseline.

to.description: A component id in the new run.

evidence.description: Free text: why they are the same.

summary.description: What changed against the baseline it replaced, for example '2 removed, 1 added, 0 changed', or 'first save'.

BaselineReport.description: Output of `traceqa diff --against ... --format json`: one entry per baseline target, with a DiffFile whose side A is the baseline and side B the run, and the result of the gate.

failOn.description: The --fail-on tokens in effect, sorted. Known values: removed, added, changed, disabled, hidden, covered, paired.

failed.description: True when at least one entry matched a token (the exit code is then 1).

BaselineTargetReport.description: The comparison of one baseline target. Exactly one of diff and error is set.

error.description: Why the target could not be compared, for example that the run has no such target.
